about:
Imricor Medical Systems was co-founded by Steve Wedan in 2006 and established in the Twin Cities area, with its headquarters in Burnsville, Minnesota. The company began with Wedan and three other pioneers aiming to bring interventional magnetic resonance (iMR) technology to the catheter ablation market. It is publicly traded on the Australian Securities Exchange (ASX:IMR).

The company develops and manufactures MR-compatible products for interventional MR procedures, including capital equipment such as the NorthStar Mapping System and the Advantage-MR EP Recorder/Stimulator, as well as single-use devices like the Vision-MR Ablation Catheter 2.0, Vision-MR Diagnostic Catheter, and steerable sheaths. Operations are based in a Burnsville facility housing research, development, quality, and commercial teams.

Imricor serves the cardiac ablation, electrophysiology, and interventional cardiology markets, supplying hospitals and cardiac centers worldwide. Early commercial customers include Dresden Heart Centre in Germany, Rady Children's Hospital in San Diego, Amsterdam UMC, Lausanne University Hospital in Switzerland, and Haga Hospital in the Netherlands. Distribution partnerships extend to Philips, GE HealthCare, and Regional Health Care Group for Australia and New Zealand.

The company was founded to replace x-ray fluoroscopy with real-time MR guidance during cardiac ablation, leveraging MRI's superior soft-tissue imaging to improve procedural safety and efficacy. Its stated mission remains the improvement of ablation therapy for patients globally, supported by CE Mark approvals in Europe, TGA approval in Australia, and FDA clearance for select products in the United States.
